title: SIDH secret-isogeny recovery

problem.name_latex: SIDH secret-isogeny recovery with torsion images
problem.name: SIDH secret-isogeny recovery with torsion images
problem.statement_latex: Given a supersingular starting curve $E_0$, a secret isogeny image $E_A$, and the published images $\phi_A(P_B),\phi_A(Q_B)$ of a basis of coprime torsion, recover the kernel of the secret isogeny $\phi_A$ of prescribed smooth degree. This input is the public-key recovery problem of SIDH and SIKE. The comparison uses quantum isogeny-oracle calls and the resulting gate cost, and classical bit complexity on the full SIDH public key.
problem.statement_text: Given a supersingular starting curve $E_0$, a secret isogeny image $E_A$, and the published images $\phi_A(P_B),\phi_A(Q_B)$ of a basis of coprime torsion, recover the kernel of the secret isogeny $\phi_A$ of prescribed smooth degree. This input is the public-key recovery problem of SIDH and SIKE. The comparison uses quantum isogeny-oracle calls and the resulting gate cost, and classical bit complexity on the full SIDH public key.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(p^{1/6})$ isogeny-oracle calls, Tani claw finding applied to split isogenies.
quantum.details_latex: In the balanced SIDH parameter regime, the two half-isogeny lists contain about $p^{1/4}$ candidates each. Quantum claw search identifies matching intermediate endpoints; the stated exponent counts isogeny evaluations with the required coherent list access. Arithmetic and memory-access factors enter the full gate cost.

classical.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log p)$, Castryck--Decru and Robert SIDH key recovery.
classical.details_latex: The full public key includes torsion images, which supply the extra information used by product-isogeny attacks. Robert's higher-dimensional abelian-variety framework gives polynomial-time key recovery in the specified SIDH setting. The polynomial algorithm recovers the prescribed secret isogeny or equivalent secret-key information from the same explicit public input.

strength.description_latex: The problem has a polynomial-time classical solution; the exponential quantum claw bound has no speedup over this comparator.

evidence.description_latex: The classical key-recovery theorem determines the comparison for SIDH public keys with their auxiliary torsion data.

hardware.description_latex: The quantum claw approach requires exponentially large coherent data structures and deep reversible isogeny arithmetic. The polynomial-time attack uses classical computation. For the quantum construction, both coherent memory and total circuit depth determine the required fault-tolerant resources.
